results.name: shared_contained_digit_other_ending_yes
results.description: For 2+ example sets in which every example contains some digit d, yes rate on non-example targets that contain such a d but whose last digit matches no example's last digit; observed > null means people use "contains digit d" more than the model predicts, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: shared_contained_digit_other_ending_yes
# description: For 2+ example sets in which every example contains some digit d, yes rate on non-example targets that contain such a d but whose last digit matches no example's last digit; observed > null means people use "contains digit d" more than the model predicts, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    tt, to = (t // 10), (t % 10)
    hit = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for dg in range(10):
        has = ((ex % 10 == dg) | ((ex // 10 == dg) & (ex >= 10) & (ex < 100)) | ((dg == 1) & (ex == 100)) | ((dg == 0) & (ex == 100)) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1)
        thas = (to == dg) | ((tt == dg) & (t >= 10) & (t < 100)) | ((t == 100) & ((dg == 1) | (dg == 0)))
        hit = hit | (has & thas)
    lastmatch = (ex % 10).eq(to, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    sel = hit & (n >= 2) & ~inset & ~lastmatch
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float)[sel].mean())

results.name: upward_minus_downward_near
results.description: For non-example targets within 15 of their nearest example, yes rate when the target is above that example minus when it is below; observed > null means people generalise more upward than the model's roughly symmetric intervals predict, observed < null means more downward.
results.code:
# name: upward_minus_downward_near
# description: For non-example targets within 15 of their nearest example, yes rate when the target is above that example minus when it is below; observed > null means people generalise more upward than the model's roughly symmetric intervals predict, observed < null means more downward.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    diff = ex.rsub(t, axis=0)  # target - example
    ad = diff.abs()
    mn = ad.min(axis=1)
    # signed diff to nearest example (ties: prefer any above)
    near_up = (diff.gt(0) & ad.eq(mn, axis=0)).any(axis=1)
    near_dn = (diff.lt(0) & ad.eq(mn, axis=0)).any(axis=1)
    ok = (mn > 0) & (mn <= 15)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    up = ok & near_up & ~near_dn
    dn = ok & near_dn & ~near_up
    if up.sum() == 0 or dn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[up].mean() - r[dn].mean())

results.name: square_set_nonexample_yes
results.description: For 2+ example sets made only of perfect squares (1..100), yes rate on non-example targets; observed > null means people generalise more broadly after square sets than the model (whose penalised square concept pushes it to other hypotheses), observed < null means less broadly.
results.code:
# name: square_set_nonexample_yes
# description: For 2+ example sets made only of perfect squares (1..100), yes rate on non-example targets; observed > null means people generalise more broadly after square sets than the model (whose penalised square concept pushes it to other hypotheses), observed < null means less broadly.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    allsq = (ex.isin([k * k for k in range(1, 11)]) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    sel = allsq & ~inset
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float)[sel].mean())

results.name: parity_only_far_target_yes
results.description: For 2+ example sets of uniform parity, yes rate on non-example same-parity targets that are >10 from every example, share no digit with any example, and are not multiples of any m in 3..10 dividing all examples (only "even"/"odd" licenses them); observed < null means the model over-uses bare parity rules, observed > null means it under-uses them.
results.code:
# name: parity_only_far_target_yes
# description: For 2+ example sets of uniform parity, yes rate on non-example same-parity targets that are >10 from every example, share no digit with any example, and are not multiples of any m in 3..10 dividing all examples (only "even"/"odd" licenses them); observed < null means the model over-uses bare parity rules, observed > null means it under-uses them.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    par = ex % 2
    unif = (par.eq(par[0], axis=0) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    samepar = (t % 2) == par[0]
    dist = ex.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    def digs(x):
        tens = (x // 10) % 10
        return [x % 10, tens.where(x >= 10)]
    td = digs(t)
    sharedig = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for col in ex.columns:
        for a in digs(ex[col]):
            for b in td:
                sharedig = sharedig | (a == b)
    mult = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for mm in range(3, 11):
        allm = ((ex % mm == 0) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1)
        mult = mult | (allm & (t % mm == 0))
    sel = unif & samepar & ~inset & (dist > 10) & ~sharedig & ~mult
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float)[sel].mean())

results.name: single_example_far_yes
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate on targets more than 10 away from the example; observed > null means people generalise from one number to distant numbers (via rules) more than the model, observed < null means the model over-generalises from a single example.
results.code:
# name: single_example_far_yes
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate on targets more than 10 away from the example; observed > null means people generalise from one number to distant numbers (via rules) more than the model, observed < null means the model over-generalises from a single example.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",")
    e = pd.to_numeric(s.where(single), errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    sel = single & ((t - e).abs() > 10)
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float)[sel].mean())

results.name: shared_last_digit_target_yes
results.description: For 2+ example sets whose examples all end in the same digit, yes rate on non-example targets ending in that digit; observed > null means people extend the "ends in d" rule more than the model (model under-weights final-digit rules), observed < null means less.

# name: shared_last_digit_target_yes
# description: For 2+ example sets whose examples all end in the same digit, yes rate on non-example targets ending in that digit; observed > null means people extend the "ends in d" rule more than the model (model under-weights final-digit rules), observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
results.description: For 2+ example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the first-shown example (but not the last) minus targets within 10 of the last-shown example (but not the first); the model is order-invariant, so observed > null means a primacy advantage and observed < null a recency advantage.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
# description: For 2+ example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the first-shown example (but not the last) minus targets within 10 of the last-shown example (but not the first); the model is order-invariant, so observed > null means a primacy advantage and observed < null a recency advantage.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    idx = (n - 1).clip(lower=0).astype(int).to_numpy()
    last = pd.Series(ex.to_numpy()[np.arange(len(ex)), idx], index=df.index)
    first = ex[0]
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nf = (t - first).abs() <= 10
    nl = (t - last).abs() <= 10
    base = (n >= 2) & ~inset
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = base & nf & ~nl
    b = base & nl & ~nf
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
